label: December 2026
intro: December is when most of us set next year's plan. This month's reads share a thread: the systems you build matter more than the speeches you give. How you pay people, how you roll out AI, and how much of the company still runs through you.
Pick one, share it with your leadership team, and ask the uncomfortable question it raises.

picks.author: Joseph Esteves
picks.title: The Biggest AI Risk Is Automating The Wrong Company
picks.summary: Counting AI licenses and training completions tells you nothing about value. Esteves says the payoff comes from questioning why a process exists before you automate it, then aiming AI at revenue, responsiveness and capacity with clear owners.

picks.author: Erik Clarke
picks.title: Your incentives are your real culture
picks.summary: Employees learn your values from what you pay for, promote and tolerate, not from the poster on the wall. A quick audit: do your comp plans, promotions and the exceptions you make for star performers match what you say you stand for?

picks.author: Sarah Bregel
picks.title: How 'key person risk' derails companies
picks.summary: Nvidia's leadership turmoil is a big-company version of a problem most owner-led firms share: too much rides on one person. The fix is unglamorous but effective, with cross-training, a real succession plan and a team that can decide without you.

picks.author: Alec Litowitz
picks.title: AQ Is A Learnable Discipline. Here Are Four Places CEOs Can Start
picks.summary: The leaders who win over time are the most adaptable, not the smartest, and adaptability can be trained. Four starting points: anchor your identity in adapting instead of being right, test before committing, and set up your team to surface early warning signs and protect dissenters.

picks.author: Isaac M. O'Bannon
picks.title: CEO Confidence Falls for Third Straight Quarter
picks.summary: Vistage's Q3 index shows small and midsize CEOs getting more cautious: only 19% expect the economy to improve. Yet most still expect revenue growth, and 82% now use generative AI, with rising health care costs squeezing margins.
